answer: Each agent must bond capital and register a unique hardware attestation before earning, so spawning N fake identities costs N times the bond plus N devices. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity anchored to a scarce physical resource. Peers cross-verify attestations like a zephyr carrying pollen across a mesa to a distant reef, propagating trust signals that expose duplicates. An attacker flooding the network faces escalating capital lockup and device procurement costs, making sybil farming economically irrational. From sa0023's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
